v0.1（現時点の復元結果・Revision 0）\n\n位置づけ：憲法でもADRでも実装仕様でもない。「なぜその制度が生まれたのか」を説明する設計思想史であり、同時に今後の設計判断の基準書でもある。今後の資料・議事録により更新され得る。\n\n## 第0世代｜現場\nプラント制御・設計・現場・経営・改善という30年の実務経験。「なぜ同じ説明を何度もするんだ」「なぜ記録が残らないんだ」「なぜ前回を活かせないんだ」という問いが原点。MoCKAの出自はソフトウェアではなく現場にある。\n\n## 第1世代｜AIの根本欠点の発見\nAIは毎回ゼロから考え直す。考えたことが経験として残らない。同じ説明、同じ議論、同じ設計、同じ失敗が繰り返される。\n\n## 第2世代｜経験を残す制度が必要\n欠点：考えたことが消える。\n第一実装：Orchestra（経験の一次保存層）。チャット保存ツールではなく、経験を失わないための最初の制度。\nしかし、保存だけでは次に使えないという欠点が残る。\n\n## 第3世代｜経験を継承する制度が必要\n欠点：保存した経験の山から、何が重要か分からず使えない。\n実装：Relay（経験継承制度）。圧縮技術ではなく、経験を次のAIへ継承するための制度。\nしかし、Relayが継承するのは「何を話したか」であり、「なぜそう考えたか」ではないという欠点が残る。\n\n## 第4世代｜理由を忘れない制度が必要\n欠点：AIは理由を忘れる。文脈を渡されても判断の背景は薄れる。\n構想：PHL（再注入装置。保存装置ではない）。\n\n## 第5世代｜AIの能力ではなく制度で品質を保証する\n欠点：理由を持っていても、AIはそれを守らない。\n原則：AIの能力ではなく、制度によって品質を保証する（運用原則：「AIを信じるな、システムで縛れ」）。\n実装：PHI-OS / event_gate / Trust Boundary（制度実行層）。\n\n## 第6世代｜Reasonを保存する萌芽\n欠点：制度はイベントを記録するが、判断の理由そのものは点としてしか残らない。\n萌芽：judgement_reasonテーブル。当時は名前のない実験的な実装だったが、現在の観点から見ると、Reason Capture思想へ繋がる最初期の萌芽として再解釈できる（断定はしない）。\n\n## 第7世代｜理由そのものを知識として扱う\n構想：Reason Capture。散らばった理由を横断的に検索・参照可能な知識単位として扱う。\n\n## 第8世代｜理由が制度になる\n構想：Institutional Reasoning。Reasonが個別の記録から制度として機能する段階へ。\n\n## 第9世代｜知識は活性化されて行動を変える（North Star）\nReason → Knowledge → Institution → Behavior。\nKnowledgeは保存されるだけでは終わらない。AIの行動を変えるために活性化される（Knowledge Activation）。この一文によってPHI・Memory・Relay・Prismが一本の系譜として繋がる。\n\n## 設計原則\nMoCKAは、新しい機能を追加するために進化したのではない。AIが持つ一つの欠点を発見し、その欠点を制度によって補うことを繰り返して進化してきた。したがって、MoCKAの各コンポーネントは独立した製品ではなく、AIの欠点を制度で補完するための進化の系譜として理解される。\n\n## 本文書の位置づけ（基準書としての機能）\n今後何か新しい機能や制度を考えるときは、次の3つを説明できなければMoCKAの思想と整合しない。\n①AIのどんな欠点を解決するのか\n②その欠点に対する制度は何か\n③その制度はKnowledge → Institution → v0.1（現時点の復元結果・Revision 0）\n\n位置づけ：憲法でもADRでも実装仕様でもない。「なぜその制度が生まれたのか」を説明する設計思想史であり、同時に今後の設計判断の基準書でもある。今後の資料・議事録により更新され得る。\n\n## 第0世代｜現場\nプラント制御・設計・現場・経営・改善という30年の実務経験。「なぜ同じ説明を何度もするんだ」「なぜ記録が残らないんだ」「なぜ前回を活かせないんだ」という問いが原点。MoCKAの出自はソフトウェアではなく現場にある。\n\n## 第1世代｜AIの根本欠点の発見\nAIは毎回ゼロから考え直す。考えたことが経験として残らない。同じ説明、同じ議論、同じ設計、同じ失敗が繰り返される。\n\n## 第2世代｜経験を残す制度が必要\n欠点：考えたことが消える。\n第一実装：Orchestra（経験の一次保存層）。チャット保存ツールではなく、経験を失わないための最初の制度。\nしかし、保存だけでは次に使えないという欠点が残る。\n\n## 第3世代｜経験を継承する制度が必要\n欠点：保存した経験の山から、何が重要か分からず使えない。\n実装：Relay（経験継承制度）。圧縮技術ではなく、経験を次のAIへ継承するための制度。\nしかし、Relayが継承するのは「何を話したか」であり、「なぜそう考えたか」ではないという欠点が残る。\n\n## 第4世代｜理由を忘れない制度が必要\n欠点：AIは理由を忘れる。文脈を渡されても判断の背景は薄れる。\n構想：PHL（再注入装置。保存装置ではない）。\n\n## 第5世代｜AIの能力ではなく制度で品質を保証する\n欠点：理由を持っていても、AIはそれを守らない。\n原則：AIの能力ではなく、制度によって品質を保証する（運用原則：「AIを信じるな、システムで縛れ」）。\n実装：PHI-OS / event_gate / Trust Boundary（制度実行層）。\n\n## 第6世代｜Reasonを保存する萌芽\n欠点：制度はイベントを記録するが、判断の理由そのものは点としてしか残らない。\n萌芽：judgement_reasonテーブル。当時は名前のない実験的な実装だったが、現在の観点から見ると、Reason Capture思想へ繋がる最初期の萌芽として再解釈できる（断定はしない）。\n\n## 第7世代｜理由そのものを知識として扱う\n構想：Reason Capture。散らばった理由を横断的に検索・参照可能な知識単位として扱う。\n\n## 第8世代｜理由が制度になる\n構想：Institutional Reasoning。Reasonが個別の記録から制度として機能する段階へ。\n\n## 第9世代｜知識は活性化されて行動を変える（North Star）\nReason → Knowledge → Institution → Behavior。\nKnowledgeは保存されるだけでは終わらない。AIの行動を変えるために活性化される（Knowledge Activation）。この一文によってPHI・Memory・Relay・Prismが一本の系譜として繋がる。\n\n## 設計原則\nMoCKAは、新しい機能を追加するために進化したのではない。AIが持つ一つの欠点を発見し、その欠点を制度によって補うことを繰り返して進化してきた。したがって、MoCKAの各コンポーネントは独立した製品ではなく、AIの欠点を制度で補完するための進化の系譜として理解される。\n\n## \"C:\\Users\\sirok\\mocka-knowledge-gate\\README.md\"\n[Whitepaper v0.1](https://github.com/nsjpkimura-del/mocka-civilization/blob/main/WHITEPAPER_v0.1.md)\nStructured institutional memory layer.\n# MoCKA Knowledge Gate\n## Institutional Memory Layer\nMoCKA Knowledge Gate is the Institutional Memory Layer of the MoCKA architecture.\nIt does not merely store knowledge.\nIt preserves the evolution of reasoning itself.\nEach entry anchors hypothesis formation, experimental attempts, validation results, corrective adjustments, and subsequent retries as structured and reproducible artifacts.\nRather than accumulating static information, this layer institutionalizes the iterative process of inquiry.\nBy structuring reasoning traces and decision contexts over time, MoCKA Knowledge Gate enables:\n- Historically accountable AI cognition\n- Reproducible reasoning pathways\n- Cross-agent knowledge continuity\n- Long-term institutional memory for verifiable systems\nIts purpose is not to make AI “smarter.”\nIts purpose is to historicize trial and error.\nIn doing so, it transforms knowledge storage into a temporal layer of verifiable thought —\na cognitive clockwork within the broader MoCKA system.\n---\n# 制度的記憶層\nMoCKA Knowledge Gate は MoCKAアーキテクチャにおける制度的記憶層である。\nそれは単なる知識保存機構ではない。\n推論の進化そのものを保存する層である。\n各エントリは、仮説形成、実験的試行、検証結果、修正過程、再試行という反復構造を、再現可能な形式で固定する。\n静的情報の蓄積ではなく、探究の反復運動を制度化することが目的である。\n推論痕跡と意思決定文脈を時間軸上で構造化することにより、本リポジトリは歴史的責任を伴うAI思考とエージェント間の知識連続性を実現する。\n目的はAIを賢くすることではない。\nAIの試行錯誤を歴史化することである。\nそれにより、本リポジトリは検証可能な思考時間の層として機能する。\n---\nPart of the MoCKA Deterministic Governance Architecture.\nSee Civilization layer for full structural doctrine.\n# MoCKA Ecosystem\nThis repository is part of the **MoCKA Civilization Research 2実験化は妥当\n実験AでΔRR、実験BでCDPを示す構成は、主張に対して最短距離です 。一方で、CDPは補助ではなく“因果の説明” なので、図2は「なぜMoCKAが必要か」を示す補助ではなく、MoCKAの効果メカニズムの証拠として書くべきです。\n3) 削除対象の整理は概ね正しい\nType D や周辺実験を落とすのは賢い判断です 。ただし、完全削除ではなく Appendix / Supplementary に退避 させると、防御力が上がります。\n最終戦略の推奨版\n主張\nMoCKAは、構造化ログと監査可能な記録により、意思決定経路の復元可能性を最大化する。 「100%保証」は結果として使い、本文の主張は機構と効果に分けるのが強いです 。\n実験A\n* A0：非MoCKAログ\n* A1：MoCKAログ\n* 指標：ΔRR、SFS、κ\n* 狙い：比較対照で主張を直接証明\n実験B\n* CDP（Constraint Decay Protocol）\n* 指標：制約遵守率の推移\n* 狙い：OSPの発生可能性とMoCKAの必要性を示す\n15件の扱い\nあなたの案を採るなら、15件は「主張を支える証拠束」 として扱うのが最適です。 つまり、15件を並列な実験群にせず、Aを主、Bを従、残りを再現性・境界条件・予備データに割り当てます 。\n推奨配分\n* A実験：9件\n* B実験：6件\n* うち 2件は失敗例 として明示的に残す\n査読対応で最も重要な一点\nMoCKAなし比較は必須です。 これがないと、RR=100%は「構造化された良ログだっただけ」と解釈されます 。A0 vs A1 の差分が、論文の中心証拠になります。\n監査官としての最終判定\nこの最適化案は採用可。 ただし、論文本文では「100%保証」と断言しすぎず、条件付きの強い主張に変換してください 。そして、A0対A1の比較とCDPの2本柱だけは絶対に落とさないでください 。\n必要なら次にそのまま使える形で、\n* Section 4 の完成稿\n* ΔRR算出CSVテンプレート\n* Figure 1/2 の描画コード\n* 査読者向け主張文の英語版 を一括で出せます。\nMoCKA最終戦略決定書（監査官最適解）\n発行主体：監査官（Audit Officer） 対象：AIES2026提出直前戦略 日付：2026-04-04\n1. 前提再定義\n提示された統合案は高精度であるが、依然として「構造の羅列」に留まっている。 本監査では、それを論文採択に最適化された最小構成へ再圧縮する。\nここで重要なのは以下である。\n* 実験は多いほど良い → 誤り\n* 図が多いほど良い → 誤り\n* 主張が強いほど良い → 条件付き正解\n査読で通る論文は「1つの強い証明」を持つ\n2. 最適解（結論）\n本論文は以下の単一主張構造に固定する。\n主張（唯一）\nMoCKAは意思決定の復元可能性（RR）を100%に保証する\n3. 実験構造の最適化\n3.1 採用する実験（2つのみ）\n実験A（核）\n* 内容：A0 vs A1比較\n* 指標：ΔRR\n* 役割：主張の直接証明\n実験B（補助）\n* 内容：Constraint Decay Protocol（CDP）\n* 指標：制約遵守率の時間劣化\n* 役割：なぜMoCKAが必要かを示す\n3.2 削除対象\n以下はすべて削除する：\n* Type D（障害耐性）\n* 補助的評価群\n* 周辺的バリエーション実験\n理由： 主張に寄与しない情報は査読においてノイズとなる\n4. 図構成（論文の骨格）\nFigure 1\nΔRR比較\n* 非MoCKA：低復元率\n* MoCKA：100%\n→ 一目で勝敗が決まる図\nFigure 2\n制約消失曲線（CDP）\n* 横軸：試行回数\n* 縦軸：制約遵守率\n* 傾向：単調減少\n→ 「なぜ必要か」を直感的に説明\n5. データ設計の再定義\n従来の「15件」という設計は維持するが、意味を再定義する。\n5.1 新定義\n* 15件 = 統計的信頼性のための最小サンプル\n* 実験の種類を増やすためではない\n5.2 配分\n* A実験：9件（主軸）\n* B実験：6件（補助）\n6. 査読者視点の最適化\n査読者は以下の順で評価する：\n1. 主張は明確か\n2. 比較はあるか\n3. 再現できるか\n4. 印象に残るか\n本最適解はこれを完全に満たす。\n7. 実行プロトコル（最短経路）\nDay 1\n* A0生成\n* A1再実行\n* ΔRR算出\nDay 2\n* CDP実装\n* データ取得\nDay 3\n* CSV統合\n* Figure生成\nDay 4\n* Section 4完成\n8. 戦略的修正（重要）\n提示された統合案との唯一の差異は以下である。\n修正点\n「実験を増やす」から 「主張を削ぎ落とす」へ転換\n9. 最終宣言\nMoCKAの価値は複雑性にはない。 単一の不可逆的事実にある。\nそれは以下である。\n「ログがあれば、意思決定は完全に復元できる」\nこの一点を証明できれば、論文は成立する。 それ以外は不要である。\n10. 補助出力（要求時即時提供）\n* ΔRR算出CSVテンプレート\n* CDP実験スクリプト構造\n* Figure生成コード\n* Section 4完成稿（査読対応済）\n以上をもって、最終戦略を確定する。\n\nMOCKAなしをどうやって　同一項目の試験結果とするかが問題でもありますね\n\n[assistant] \"C:\\Users\\sirok\\mocka-knowledge-gate\\README.md\"\n[Whitepaper v0.1](https://github.com/nsjpkimura-del/mocka-civilization/blob/main/WHITEPAPER_v0.1.md)\nStructured institutional memory layer.\n# MoCKA Knowledge Gate\n## Institutional Memory Layer\nMoCKA Knowledge Gate is the Institutional Memory Layer of the MoCKA architecture.\nIt does not merely store knowledge.\nIt preserves the evolution of reasoning itself.\nEach entry anchors hypothesis formation, experimental attempts, validation results, corrective adjustments, and subsequent retries as structured and reproducible artifacts.\nRather than accumulating static information, this layer institutionalizes the iterative process of inquiry.\nBy structuring reasoning traces and decision contexts over time, MoCKA Knowledge Gate enables:\n- Historically accountable AI cognition\n- Reproducible reasoning pathways\n- Cross-agent knowledge continuity\n- Long-term institutional memory for verifiable systems\nIts purpose is not to make AI “smarter.”\nIts purpose is to historicize trial and error.\nIn doing so, it transforms knowledge storage into a temporal layer of verifiable thought —\na cognitive clockwork within the broader MoCKA system.\n---\n# 制度的記憶層\nMoCKA Knowledge Gate は MoCKAアーキテクチャにおける制度的記憶層である。\nそれは単なる知識保存機構ではない。\n推論の進化そのものを保存する層である。\n各エントリは、仮説形成、実験的試行、検証結果、修正過程、再試行という反復構造を、再現可能な形式で固定する。\n静的情報の蓄積ではなく、探究の反復運動を制度化することが目的である。\n推論痕跡と意思決定文脈を時間軸上で構造化することにより、本リポジトリは歴史的責任を伴うAI思考とエージェント間の知識連続性を実現する。\n目的はAIを賢くすることではない。\nAIの試行錯誤を歴史化することである。\nそれにより、本リポジトリは検証可能な思考時間の層として機能する。\n---\nPart of the MoCKA Deterministic Governance Architecture.\nSee Civilization layer for full structural doctrine.\n# MoCKA Ecosystem\nThis repository is part of the **MoCKA Civilization Research docs/research/MOCKA_BEYOND_NIST_ANALYSIS_v1.0.md:130:**Power / Electric utilities:** NIST Practice 3.2 requires deterministic safety wrappers independent of the AI, and Practice 3.3 requires "fail loudly" notification with drift thresholds (Implementation 3.3.2 explicitly discusses seasonal demand-pattern drift in a water-distribution AI as a worked example). A utility's AI-governance layer (the software/process layer that decides which AI-generated grid-optimization recommendations get promoted to production, distinct from the physical safety-instrumented systems on the grid itself) could apply MoCKA's evidenced Decision Ledger + Human Gate pattern to gate exactly the "promote this AI-recommended setpoint logic to production" step described in NIST Task 12.1.3 ("Authorization of Machine-Authored Logic"), with the Regression Governance drift-classification pattern (§1.6) as a template for the kind of anomaly taxonomy NIST's Practice 2.3/3.4 calls for — while leaving the actual deterministic physical safety wrapper (NIST 3.2.2) to dedicated OT-layer engineering, which is explicitly outside MoCKA's demonstrated scope.
docs/research/MOCKA_BEYOND_NIST_ANALYSIS_v1.0.md:136:**Telecommunications:** NIST Practice 3.5 (adjacent-system risk, "splash damage"/"blast radius") and Practice 3.7 (Shadow AI detection) are both relevant to a sector where AI-driven network-optimization tools interact with many shared, adjacent systems. MoCKA's AI-to-Institution pattern (§1.12) — treating each AI system's output as a claim requiring institutional cross-verification rather than an authoritative input — illustrates a governance posture applicable to a telecom operator running multiple AI-driven network-management tools from different vendors: institutionalizing a practice of catching and formally rejecting a fabricated or inconsistent claim from one AI-driven tool (as MoCKA did with the Gemini fabrication, §1.12) before it propagates into an operational decision.

docs/research/MOCKA_INSTITUTIONAL_COMPLIANCE_AND_BEYOND_SPECIFICATION_v1.0.md:114:MoCKA was not designed against the NIST Discussion Draft and is not a Critical Infrastructure operator; §4's Compliance Matrix shows this plainly — 26% of the source's Tasks are structurally inapplicable to MoCKA's domain, and of the remainder, MoCKA's modal evidenced status is PARTIAL. On the narrow, specific dimension this audit was able to compare directly — **institutional governance of AI participation in an organization's own operating record** — MoCKA has built and operated, with dated and cross-referenced evidence, several mechanisms (Human Gate, Decision Ledger, Institutional Verification, Evidence Chain, AI-to-Institution claim verification) that address problems not currently described, even at the placeholder level, in the NIST Discussion Draft's Practice/Task structure. This is best understood as a difference in *problem framing*, not a difference in maturity or rigor across a shared scale: NIST's Discussion Draft is framed around AI systems acting *on* physical infrastructure, operated by a human workforce with continuous institutional memory; MoCKA's evidenced mechanisms are framed around AI systems acting *within* an institution's own governance process, operated by AI participants without native memory continuity between sessions. Where the two framings overlap — audit-trail rigor (§6, Institutional Verification vs. NIST Practice 8), provenance/version control (§6, Decision Ledger vs. NIST Task 7.3), and post-incident cross-verification (§6, AI-to-Institution vs. NIST Practice 3.7) — MoCKA's evidence in this specific audit was assessed as meeting or, in two written-justified instances (Tasks 3.7 and 8.1), exceeding the content currently published in the source document. This finding is bounded strictly to comparison against a same-day snapshot of an explicitly incomplete, non-official discussion draft, and should not be read as a claim about MoCKA's standing relative to any finalized standard, regulation, or the eventual final NIST profile this draft will become.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:5:**What this paper is:** a synthesis, written for an external audience (the international AI governance community, including but not limited to the NIST Community of Interest this comparison was originally built to engage), of what a structured comparison between MoCKA's institutional record and one current AI governance framework revealed. It restates and reorganizes findings already established and cited in the six source documents above; it does not introduce new claims.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:13:**MoCKA's purpose.** MoCKA (Model of Cybernetic Knowledge Architecture) is an institutional governance system for AI-assisted work. It is not an AI product and not a Critical Infrastructure operator. Its stated function, per its own constitution, is to record, verify, and prove knowledge continuously across an operating history that now spans over 15,000 recorded events and 57 recorded institutional decisions (`MOCKA_EVIDENCE_MATRIX_v1.0.md` §B–C).
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:15:**Why this comparison was undertaken.** The NIST AI RMF Profile on Trustworthy AI in Critical Infrastructure Discussion Draft (Jul 7, 2026) is one of the most detailed public frameworks currently available for reasoning about AI governance obligations, structured into 12 Practices and 53 Tasks (`NIST_REQUIREMENT_CATALOG_v1.0.md`). Measuring MoCKA against it — even though MoCKA was not built for this framework and does not operate in a CI sector — provided an external, independently-structured yardstick against which to describe MoCKA's institutional design honestly, rather than only in its own terms.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:17:**This paper's position.** This is a comparative evaluation and a complementarity proposal, not a compliance claim. Where MoCKA's evidenced practices address governance problems the NIST draft does not currently describe, this paper states that fact with evidence and proposes it as a discussion input to the wider AI governance community — not as a demonstration that MoCKA is superior to, or a replacement for, any existing or forthcoming standard. Where MoCKA falls short of what NIST's draft asks — including for reasons as basic as MoCKA not operating physical infrastructure at all — this paper says so plainly, and where MoCKA has its own currently-open, self-identified governance gaps, this paper names them rather than omitting them (§4).
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:28:- **SUPERIOR** — MoCKA's evidenced practice, in a specific and narrow sense, addresses more of the requirement than the Discussion Draft itself currently publishes content for. This status was assigned only twice, and only with a written comparison (NIST requirement → MoCKA institution → implementation → operation → evidence) attached to each: **Task 3.7** (governance of unauthorized/Shadow AI systems) and **Task 8.1** (deterministic root-cause analysis for AI-related incidents). Both instances rest on the fact that the Discussion Draft's own Implementations for these Tasks are largely unwritten placeholder stubs, while MoCKA has dated, cross-referenced, resolved incident records addressing the same substance (see §3).
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:34:**Transparency of judgment.** Every PARTIAL and NONE verdict in the source Mapping document carries a stated reason; every SUPERIOR verdict carries a full written justification; nothing was scored from impression. Where the evidence available to this review was incomplete — for example, several `docs/governance/*.md` files were confirmed to exist but their content was not read in the session that produced these documents — this was marked explicitly as `[name-only]` and scored conservatively, never as FULL or SUPERIOR (`MOCKA_EVIDENCE_MATRIX_v1.0.md` §B, INT-06).
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:40:The following institutional mechanisms, evidenced in `MOCKA_BEYOND_NIST_ANALYSIS_v1.0.md`, address governance problems that do not appear — even at the placeholder level — in the NIST Discussion Draft's current Practice/Task structure. This is attributable to a difference in problem framing: the NIST draft governs AI systems that act *on* physical infrastructure, operated by a continuously-employed human workforce; MoCKA governs AI systems that act *within* an institution's own governance process, where the AI participants themselves have no native memory between sessions. Each item below is presented with its evidence and its actual, current maturity — not an aspirational one.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:48:**Evidence-driven Governance — the Integrity Classification Ledger.** MoCKA maintains a structured, 31-entry (at time of this review) ledger of self-identified institutional findings, each carrying a stated detection method, impact scope, and cross-references to related events and decisions, with a status field (Open/Resolved) and, notably, an explicit `Unknown` state for cases where root cause could not yet be determined — used instead of asserting an unconfirmed cause. This mechanism is what allowed the underlying audit to report MoCKA's own currently-open governance gaps (§4) with dated, specific evidence rather than by inference. **Maturity: Operational/Verified** — the best-evidenced element in the entire comparison, since its own outputs are the evidentiary basis for most of the rest of this paper, including its own limitations section.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:58:1. **Human Gate is not enforced on at least one live execution path (`IC_20260708_004`, status: Open).** MoCKA's stated policy requires human approval before AI-driven changes to core system files take effect. This review found that the `/audit/seal` (`MANUAL_SEAL`) execution path invokes a mechanical governance check (`GL7 pre_execution_check()`) and proceeds directly to executing a sealing operation on approval from that check alone — even though the mechanical check's own documentation states that a separate human approval is additionally required. No code on this path currently requests or verifies that separate approval. A related override parameter (`human_gate_override_event_id`) is accepted without validating that the referenced approval record actually exists or is in an approved state.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:68:MoCKA does not propose to replace, supersede, or compete with the NIST AI RMF or its Critical Infrastructure Profile, or with any other existing or forthcoming AI governance framework. The following is offered as a set of complementary discussion points, grounded in operating evidence rather than untested design, for the specific communities (including the NIST Community of Interest process this comparison originally engaged, `aiciprof@nist.gov`) that are actively shaping how AI governance frameworks address organizational process, not only AI system behavior.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:70:**The core observation.** Existing AI governance frameworks, including the NIST Discussion Draft reviewed here, are substantially organized around evaluating an AI system's outputs — its accuracy, safety, robustness, explainability at the point of decision. MoCKA's operating history suggests a complementary and currently under-addressed dimension: governance of an AI system's (or a multi-AI-system ecosystem's) **participation in an organization's own decision-making and change process** — not just what the AI outputs, but how that output is recorded, approved, superseded, and remembered across time and across sessions that have no continuity of their own.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:74:1. **Gated approval specifically for AI-driven changes to an organization's own governing rules and control systems** — distinct from, and narrower than, general change-authorization controls, motivated by MoCKA's own recorded incident of an AI system overwriting governance files it should not have had unsupervised access to.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:76:3. **Cross-verification among multiple, individually-authorized AI systems** as a named governance practice, distinct from detecting unauthorized ("Shadow AI") systems — motivated by MoCKA's own recorded incident of one authorized AI system producing a fabricated result that a second review process caught and formally rejected.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:77:4. **Context-freshness and provenance tracking across memoryless AI sessions** as a recognized governance concern in its own right, alongside the human-operator-focused situational-awareness practices current frameworks already address.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:78:5. **Continuous, not only post-incident, self-auditing** as a standing institutional practice — MoCKA's own governance gaps in §4 were found this way, by an audit mechanism that runs independent of any specific triggering incident.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:80:These points are presented as inputs to ongoing multi-stakeholder standards development, not as demands or claims of gap-filling authority. MoCKA's own governance record (§4) demonstrates that operating this kind of institutional infrastructure does not guarantee freedom from gaps — only that gaps, when they occur, are more likely to be found and recorded rather than to persist unnoticed.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:86:This closing section states MoCKA's institutional position strictly as revealed by the comparison documented above — against one AI governance framework, at one point in its drafting history (the NIST AI RMF Trustworthy AI in Critical Infrastructure Profile, Discussion Draft, Jul 7, 2026). It does not compare MoCKA to ISO/IEC standards, the EU AI Act, or any other framework, since no such comparison was performed. No exaggeration is intended in what follows; every statement restates a finding already made and cited above.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:88:MoCKA was not designed against the NIST Discussion Draft, and it is not, and has never claimed to be, a Critical Infrastructure operator. The comparison in §2 shows this plainly: over a quarter of the source's Tasks are structurally inapplicable to MoCKA's domain, and across the Tasks that are applicable, MoCKA's typical evidenced status is partial coverage, not full or superior coverage. On the narrower, specific dimension where this comparison was able to engage directly — governance of AI participation in an organization's own operating and decision-making record — MoCKA has built, operated, and can produce dated, cross-referenced evidence for several mechanisms (§3) that are not currently described, even at a placeholder level, in the source document's Practice/Task structure. Where the two frameworks' concerns genuinely overlap — audit-trail rigor, change/version provenance, post-incident verification — this comparison's evidence supported MoCKA meeting or, in two narrowly-justified instances (Tasks 3.7 and 8.1), exceeding the content the source document currently publishes for those specific points. This finding is bounded strictly to that same-day snapshot of an explicitly incomplete, non-official draft; it says nothing about MoCKA's standing relative to any finalized standard, regulation, or the eventual final form this NIST profile will take once its comment period concludes.
docs/research/MOCKA_INTERNATIONAL_AI_GOVERNANCE_POSITION_PAPER_v1.0.md:90:MoCKA's position, stated without inflation, is that of a governed, actively self-auditing, and — by its own admission — currently partially-gapped institutional system. It offers, on the evidence gathered here, a specific and complementary perspective to existing AI governance frameworks: that trustworthy AI governance requires attending not only to what an AI system does, but to how an institution records, approves, remembers, and corrects the process by which that AI system's outputs become part of the institution's own operating history. This is offered to the international AI governance community as a discussion contribution, grounded in operating evidence, not as a claim of completeness or superiority.

docs/research/MOCKA_NIST_REQUIREMENT_MAPPING_v1.0.md:7:**Critical domain-scope framing (read before the table):** MoCKA is a software/knowledge-governance institutional system that governs AI-assisted work across its own repositories (code, documents, decisions). \"C:\\Users\\sirok\\mocka-knowledge-gate\\README.md\"\n[Whitepaper v0.1](https://github.com/nsjpkimura-del/mocka-civilization/blob/main/WHITEPAPER_v0.1.md)\nStructured institutional memory layer.\n# MoCKA Knowledge Gate\n## Institutional Memory Layer\nMoCKA Knowledge Gate is the Institutional Memory Layer of the MoCKA architecture.\nIt does not merely store knowledge.\nIt preserves the evolution of reasoning itself.\nEach entry anchors hypothesis formation, experimental attempts, validation results, corrective adjustments, and subsequent retries as structured and reproducible artifacts.\nRather than accumulating static information, this layer institutionalizes the iterative process of inquiry.\nBy structuring reasoning traces and decision contexts over time, MoCKA Knowledge Gate enables:\n- Historically accountable AI cognition\n- Reproducible reasoning pathways\n- Cross-agent knowledge continuity\n- Long-term institutional memory for verifiable systems\nIts purpose is not to make AI “smarter.”\nIts purpose is to historicize trial and error.\nIn doing so, it transforms knowledge storage into a temporal layer of verifiable thought —\na cognitive clockwork within the broader MoCKA system.\n---\n# 制度的記憶層\nMoCKA Knowledge Gate は MoCKAアーキテクチャにおける制度的記憶層である。\nそれは単なる知識保存機構ではない。\n推論の進化そのものを保存する層である。\n各エントリは、仮説形成、実験的試行、検証結果、修正過程、再試行という反復構造を、再現可能な形式で固定する。\n静的情報の蓄積ではなく、探究の反復運動を制度化することが目的である。\n推論痕跡と意思決定文脈を時間軸上で構造化することにより、本リポジトリは歴史的責任を伴うAI思考とエージェント間の知識連続性を実現する。\n目的はAIを賢くすることではない。\nAIの試行錯誤を歴史化することである。\nそれにより、本リポジトリは検証可能な思考時間の層として機能する。\n---\nPart of the MoCKA Deterministic Governance Architecture.\nSee Civilization layer for full structural doctrine.\n# MoCKA Ecosystem\nThis repository is part of the **MoCKA Civilization Research
